title: Why YouTube's view counter had a limit of 2,147,483,647
description:
YouTube used to store view counts as 32-bit signed integers: 32 switches, each on or off. Every switch doubles how far you can count (10 switches reach 1,023, 20 reach about a million), but one is kept for the minus sign, so 31 switches top out at 2,147,483,647. One more view flips every switch and the count would read -2,147,483,648. On December 1, 2014, YouTube announced that Gangnam Style had passed that number and that view counts now use 64 bits, which count to about 9.2 quintillion: over a billion views for every person on Earth.

Numbers checked in code (32- and 64-bit integer limits, the overflow, and the bit flips). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangnam_Style https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population

beats.say: How many views can YouTube actually count?
It's not that computers can't count that high. The counter has a fixed number of switches.
YouTube stored every view count in 32 bits. 32 switches, each on or off.
Each switch you add doubles the count. 10 switches reach 1,023. 20 reach a million.
But the first switch is saved for the minus sign. That leaves 31.
Every switch flips, even the sign. Now it reads minus 2 billion.
In 2014, Gangnam Style passed that line.
So YouTube moved the counter to 64 bits. That counts to 9.2 quintillion.
Enough for everyone on Earth to watch it a billion times.
